inventory_scope: 110 publicly submitted papers found in repository publication receipts: R023–R041, D1–D30, November 2 (22), November 4 (28), and current batch (11). R001–R022 had no public submission receipt in this audit and are not counted.

entries.title: An 88-vertex totient realization of the four-stage contracted nanostar: a counterexample to the Ghanbari-Alikhani nanostar conjecture (arXiv:2012.12492; Math. Gazette 2023)
entries.scope: Ghanbari-Alikhani final conjecture: no nanostar grown at least four stages is a G_phi-graph. False at stage 4: 23 explicit generators give an 88-vertex orbit tree with centre 1024 isomorphic to D_4.

entries.title: Interpolation of orientable total domination by safe arc reversals: a proof of the Hansen-Lai-Yue conjecture (JCMCC 1999; Anderson-Dravec-Johnston-Kuenzel Conjecture 3.1, arXiv:2311.16307)
entries.scope: The full conjecture for all finite graphs admitting a valid orientation: every integer between dom_t(G) and DOM_t(G) is the total domination number of a valid orientation.

entries.title: A four-edge obstruction to submodular separation of quadratic Boolean monomial images: a counterexample to Brakensiek-Gopi-Guruswami Conjecture 3.33 (arXiv:1902.04740; ECCC TR19-013)
entries.scope: Conjecture 3.33 is false at (r,d) = (2,5): no integer- (indeed real-) valued submodular function on {0,1}^16 is negative exactly on the degree-2 monomial image of {0,1}^5.

entries.title: No two-round minimal line-percolating set in PG(2,5): a counterexample to Conjecture 20 of Gerbner-Keszegh-Meszaros-Patkos-Vizer (arXiv:1608.00531)
entries.scope: Conjecture 20 fails at the allowed boundary (q,r) = (5,5): in PG(2,5) no inclusion-minimal percolating set has percolation time 2 at threshold 5.

entries.title: A negative coefficient for every n >= 8 in the Alexandersson-Kebede cycle-restricted signed sum: a refutation of Conjecture 5.2.1 (Australas. J. Combin. 86(3) (2023))
entries.scope: Conjecture 5.2.1 fails at k = 3 for every n >= 8 (ordinary proof; Lean certifies n = 9 for both the version-of-record and the MathDB/arXiv v3 wording); it holds for all 2 <= k <= n when n <= 7 (computation)

entries.title: GM strategies are not a Nash equilibrium in l-player exact slow NIM(n, n-1) for n, l >= 3: a refutation of Gurvich-Naumova Conjecture 1 (arXiv:2311.03257)
entries.scope: Conjecture 1 fails for every n >= 3 and l >= 3 (ordinary block-invariant proof; Lean certifies (4,4,5)); a computed certificate at (5,5,6) shows no completion of the no-multiple convention rescues it; l = 2 is the GMMV23 theorem

entries.title: GM strategies are not a Nash equilibrium in l-player exact slow NIM(n, n-1) for n, l >= 3: a refutation of Gurvich-Naumova Conjecture 1 (arXiv:2311.03257)
entries.scope: Conjecture 1 fails for every n >= 3 and l >= 3 (ordinary block-invariant proof; Lean certifies (4,4,5)); a computed certificate at (5,5,6) shows no completion of the no-multiple convention rescues it; l = 2 is the GMMV23 theorem

entries.title: The path P_9 is an IR-graph: a nine-vertex counterexample to the Mynhardt-Roux non-IR conjecture for paths
entries.scope: part (i) of the conjecture (paths) is false: P_9 is an IR-graph; computationally 9 is the minimum order of a graph whose IR-graph is a path of order >= 3 and P_7, P_8, P_9 occur at order 9; part (ii) (cycles) and P_6 remain open

entries.title: An Euler tour of the full permutation overlap graph that no cyclic word realizes: a refutation of Hurlbert's ordering conjecture for universal cycles of permutations
entries.scope: Hurlbert's ordering conjecture (Kirsch-Sibley-Sprangel Conjecture 6.3; Hurlbert 1990; the Chung-Diaconis-Graham 1992 belief) is false at n = 4: an explicit Euler tour of the clustered overlap graph O(4) is realized by no cyclic word over any linearly ordered alphabet

entries.title: A symmetric kernel certificate for Hetyei's second-kind interval transform: a refutation of the kernel conjecture (Discrete Comput. Geom. 2024, Conjecture 39)
entries.scope: Hetyei's kernel conjecture fails at n = 5 (dim ker I_2 = 13 > 12 = dim A_5) and, computationally, at n = 6, 7; it holds for n <= 4; 347231 (Conjecture 40) fails as a remark, without separate credit

entries.title: Three induced colours on the Mobius ladder M_12: a refutation of the Lau-Shiu-Ng even Mobius ladder local antimagic conjecture
entries.scope: chi_la(M_12) = 3 (Lean certifies the failure of the value 4; the matching lower bound 3 is an ordinary odd-cycle argument), refuting Lau-Shiu-Ng Conjecture 3.2 for even n >= 4; remark: chi_la(M_8) = 3 contradicts Lau-Shiu (arXiv:2203.06594, Acta Math. Hungar. 169 (2023)) Theorem 2.4

entries.title: A rank-four nine-element counterexample to Lason common-basis conjecture
entries.scope: An actual rank4 matroid on9 labeled elements, with k2 and x1,y6, has two-base partitions of both deletions but no choices of such partitions share a base. Parallel elements permitted by source; full literal conjecture negation.

entries.title: A nonideal clutter without Kiraly choice maps
entries.scope: 11-element nonideal clutter has no p,q on clutter and full blocker satisfying membership and singleton-intersection exclusion; refutes intended nonideal-implies-choice direction
entries.label: counterexample

entries.title: A fully supported local intricacy maximum among stationary binary one-step Markov laws
entries.scope: Existence of a fully supported integer-shift-invariant stationary one-step Markov probability law on the full two-sided binary shift locally maximizing rank-zero uniform-subset intricacy relative to all stationary one-step Markov laws in the weak topology, with actual finite-limit convergence at witness and nearby comparison laws
entries.label: proof

entries.title: A Latin maximum-agreement strategy that is not optimal for the finite field objective
entries.scope: Refutes the universal Latin-implies-optimal direction of the source Definition3 finite field characterization: two nonempty Latin maximum-agreement partitions at n=5 have actual fields290<302. MathDB347712 is interpreted through its explicit source Definition3.
entries.label: counterexample

entries.title: A seven-vertex counterexample to the minimum-degree bound for Staller fast Maker-Breaker domination
entries.scope: Sevenvertex simple connected bipartite theta with branchlengths2,2,4 has minimumdegree2 and Staller-start optimalwinningnumber4>ceil(7/2)-2+1=3. Refutes Conjecture7.2(i) and thus MathDB355140 conjunction.
entries.label: counterexample

entries.title: No four-label edge coloring of K5 distinguishes all triangles by color sets
entries.scope: Every map E(K5)->Fin 4 has two distinct triangles with equal edge-color sets; refutes Pilsniak-Wozniak arXiv:2407.19050v1 Conjecture 5 (tau_s(n)=n-1 for all n>=4) at n=5. Multiset Conjecture 4 untouched.
entries.label: counterexample

entries.title: The prime field is not a maximal clique in GP(5^8,3): a counterexample to Yip's maximal subfield clique conjecture
entries.scope: For q=5^8, d=3 (largest admissible r=1), in every field of order 5^8 the prime field F_5 is a clique of GP(5^8,3) but not maximal (x=2θ+4θ^2+θ^3, f(θ)=0, f=X^8+X^7+2X^6+2). Refutes the unrestricted conjecture; ALCO Theorem 1.2 (q>(n-1)^2) untouched.
entries.label: counterexample

entries.title: Complete bipartite graphs maximise sigma_t-irregularity among connected triangle-free graphs
entries.scope: For every n>=2 and every maximiser a of a(n-a)(n-2a)^2 over 1<=a<n, K_{a,n-a} is connected, triangle-free and has sigma_t at least that of every connected triangle-free graph on n vertices; every attainer is complete bipartite with nonempty parts. Proves arXiv:2411.04881v1 Conjecture 24 / Ars Math. Contemp. 26 (2026) Conjecture 6.1 in full.
entries.label: proof

entries.title: A six-point ordinal space with the majorization property that does not embed in the real line
entries.scope: Six-point tie-free ordinal space whose identity enumeration has the Definition 7.1 majorization property for every chain length (repeats, permutations) but which admits no embedding in R; refutes Keller-Petrov Conjecture 7.4 in the range n>5 left open by the source (sufficiency proved only for n<=4).
entries.label: counterexample

entries.title: A 34-vertex maximal rigid diameter-5 subset of the eight-dimensional Hamming cube
entries.scope: Explicit 34-point subset of signed Q_8 with diameter exactly 5, inclusion-maximal subject to diameter <= 5, and a diameter partner at every point; hence b'(8;5) >= 34 > 32, refuting Briggs-Feng-Wells Conjecture 1 (b'(n;r)=2^r for n>=r).
entries.label: counterexample

entries.title: A quarter-table change from a group to a classical Moufang loop of order 16
entries.scope: F_2^4 and the cubic code loop on F_2^3 x F_2 are Moufang loops with common identity, associators with images of size 1 and 2 (inequivalent under pointed, unpointed and independent bijective readings), and table distance 64 < 3*16^2/8 = 96; refutes Drapal-Vojtechovsky Conjecture 11.2 in its stated unrestricted scope.
entries.label: counterexample

entries.title: Exact super edge-magic total strength of a seven-cycle with four leaves at one vertex
entries.scope: G(7;0,0,0,0,0,0,4) has an SEMT labeling with constant 26 (and sm=26 exactly by an ordinary degree-rearrangement bound), contradicting Deepthi Conjecture 1 sm(G(n;k_1..k_n)) = 2q+(n+3)/2 = 27 on its nonnegative leaf-count domain.
entries.label: counterexample

entries.title: An explicit non-collapsing facet of the 4 x 4 x 5 marginal cone
entries.scope: An integral functional exposes a facet of the no-three-way-interaction marginal cone P^{4,4,5} (dimension 43 in a cone of dimension 44) whose five layers have pairwise distinct zero patterns, so it is not a pullback under any state maps to 4x4x4; refutes Eriksson-Fienberg-Rinaldo-Sullivant Conjecture 14.
entries.label: counterexample

entries.title: Binary supervenience from unary supervenience on arbitrary ternary frames
entries.scope: On arbitrary ternary frames every formula of the language with two determining inputs is equivalent to one with a single determining input (guard G(A,B)=D1(A; A and B) on the four Boolean cells), so Fan Conjecture 15 (strict hierarchy) fails at n=1; the Section 7.3 relativized agreement is definable; Humberstone 2019 pp. 16-17 undefinability assertion is corrected.
entries.label: counterexample

entries.title: A wedge-complement domain with a nonstarlike Cassinian ball
entries.scope: U = C minus the closed wedge {u>=1, |v|<=(u-1)/20} is an open connected proper planar domain, starlike about 0 in both the ordinary and the strict boundary-point sense, yet its Cassinian ball B_c(0,7/4) contains 4+i and omits the midpoint 2+i/2. Klen-Mohapatra-Sahoo Conjecture 4.7 (every Cassinian ball in a starlike domain is starlike about the centre) is false for every n>=2 reading posed in the plane, under both the ordinary and the strict domain hypotheses.
entries.label: counterexample

entries.title: All corrected odd-open and even-closed XOR-magic degrees at powers of two
entries.scope: Cichacz-Grochowski-Zuazua Conjecture 25 (arXiv:2512.19278) as printed is false at every n>=4 because closed degree 2^n-4 is excluded by Proposition 24 (Batal); that correction is zero-credit. The intended conjecture (MathDB: 'apart from the degrees excluded by the previously stated nonexistence result') is proved in full: for every n>=4 there are connected simple open zero-XOR graphs on 2^n vertices of every odd degree 5..2^n-5 and closed ones of every even degree 4..2^n-6, which with Proposition 24 is the complete existence picture for the odd-open and even-closed classes.
entries.label: counterexample

entries.title: A vertex of the asymmetric subtour elimination polytope on eight nodes that is adjacent to no tour
entries.scope: Vercesi-Barta-Gambardella-Gualandi-Mastrolilli (arXiv:2506.10671) Conjecture 1 states that every vertex of P_ASEP^n has a tour in its neighbourhood. The fractional vertex x*=X/4 of P_ASEP^8 (19 support arcs, 8 tight cuts, rank 56) is adjacent to none of the 5040 tours: for each tour an integer direction certificate shows that [x*,T] is not a face. The conjecture fails at n=8; n=6,7 remain open.
entries.label: counterexample

entries.title: An adverse non-Q graph from the cyclic Latin square of order six
entries.scope: The cyclic Latin square graph of order 6 (cells of Z6xZ6 adjacent when sharing a row, column or symbol) has lambda_min = -3 and upsilon = 6, both unchanged after deleting every open neighbourhood, and no isolated vertices, so it is adverse; its stability number is 5 by the transversal parity obstruction, so it is not a Q-graph. This refutes Cardoso-Luz Conjecture 4.2 (survey arXiv:1811.05516, Optimization 69(1) 2020) that all adverse graphs are Q-graphs, also under the JCO 2016 'non complete' reading.
entries.label: counterexample

entries.title: A clique with a five-edge tail reverses the hubs-biased Kirchhoff ordering
entries.scope: Estrada-Mugnolo (J. Math. Anal. Appl. 507 (2022) 125728, arXiv:2101.07103) Conjecture 4.13 asserts R_1 >= R_0 >= R_-1 for hubs-biased Kirchhoff indices, with equality iff regular. The spectral index the authors computed (Lemma 4.6, n*tr of the group inverse) satisfies the ordering for all 12,103 connected graphs with 5<=n<=8 (independent review), but K6 with a pendant five-edge path has R_1 = 1696684/14035 < 370/3 = R_0. The literal Moore-Penrose reading (4.3) also fails there (515538204/7137235) and already fails at n=5, an uncredited source inconsistency.
entries.label: counterexample

entries.title: A parity-corrected potential proves the Elsholtz–Klahn–Lipnik four-term progression-free digit-set conjecture
entries.scope: Elsholtz-Klahn-Lipnik (Des. Codes Cryptogr. 91 (2023) 1443-1452, arXiv:2211.02588) Conjecture 2.4, repeated as Conjecture 4.6 in Lipnik's 2023 thesis: for every prime p >= 13, p = 1 mod 4, and every n divisible by (p+3)/2, S(D,n) with D = {0..(p-1)/2,(p+3)/2} has no nonconstant 4-term AP. Proved uniformly (primality unnecessary) via E(t) = 4t^2 - (3p-5)(-1)^t: the only wrapped coordinate progressions are (h-3,0,h,3) and (3,h,0,h-3), with gap 16; ordinary progressions have gap 16 s^2; equal digit frequencies force every gap to vanish.
entries.label: proof

entries.title: No order-15 circulant has diameter 2 and monophonic position number 2
entries.scope: Tuite-Thomas-Chandran (arXiv:2106.06827v3; Ars Math. Contemp. 2025) Conjecture 4.5 asserts that for every n >= 11 there is a circulant graph of order n with diameter 2 and monophonic position number 2 (still listed as open in the survey arXiv:2501.19385 v5, August 2026). False at the interior order 15. Every diameter-2 circulant of order 15 contains a triangle, or is C5[3K1] (jumps {1,4,6} or {2,3,7}) with three open twins; both kinds of triple are mp-sets. Verified circulant examples exist at every other order 11..40 (supplementary; not claimed beyond).
entries.label: counterexample

entries.title: A cubic counterexample to edge-pattern convex domination
entries.scope: Pirot-Sereni (arXiv:1904.05618; SIAM J. Discrete Math. 35(4) (2021) 2815-2843) Conjecture 2, also Conjecture 1.5.1 of Pirot's 2019 thesis, is false at d = 3, r = 2. The 8-vertex edge-rooted pattern P (root edge 01; edges 01,02,03,15,17,34,46,56: a 6-cycle with two pendants) is 3-regular, of exact depth 2 and girth 6, with e(P) = (2/5,14/5,4/5). With alpha = (1/1000,7/27,1/3), alpha.e(P) = 67027/67500 < 1, while every acyclic 3-regular depth-2 edge-rooted pattern (all 81 leaf-count forms) has alpha.e(T) >= 3001/3000. So no convex combination of tree constraints is weaker than e(P). The source's optimized bounds (Lemma 10) are unaffected.
entries.label: counterexample

entries.title: Two hook tableaux of size 12 with equal multisets of 8-minors: the k+4 reconstruction conjecture fails
entries.scope: Erickson-Herden-Meddaugh-Sepanski-Hammon-Mohn-Ruiz-Bolanos (arXiv:2307.13161; J. Combin. Theory Ser. A 209 (2025) 105950), Conjecture conj:k+4: for n >= k+4 the multiset mM_k(T) of k-minors (over all jeu de taquin deletion sequences) determines a standard Young tableau. False at k = 8, n = 12. The hooks T1 (first row 1 5 7 8 12) and T2 (first row 1 2 3 7 10 11) are distinct and have identical mM_8 (19,958,400 minors each). Supplementary (ordinary mathematics, not Lean): a hook weight formula shows that no bound n >= k + c works for any constant c, with an explicit n = k+5 failure at k = 11.
entries.label: counterexample

entries.title: Parameter concavity of the generalized inverse hyperbolic sine
entries.scope: StrictConcaveOn p>log(2)/2 for every x>0 of literal integral0..x (1+t^p)^(-1/p); resolves full p>1,0<x<1 source question
entries.label: partial_progress

entries.title: Strict convexity of Gamma-ratio level curves
entries.scope: For each c>1, unique positive height h_c(x) solving Gamma(h)Gamma(h+2x)/Gamma(h+x)^2=c for x>0, strictly convex on all x>0; source c2 included
entries.label: proof

entries.title: Exact dyadic denominator law in shifted Jacobi parameters
entries.scope: For every integer r>=1, the maximal dyadic denominator exponent of the literal kappa_r(u,v) is 2r+v2((r-1)!). Every coefficient satisfies the upper bound and the nonzero pure-u^r coefficient attains it. Odd denominator factors are allowed.
entries.label: proof

entries.title: A convergent cascade series without geometric decay
entries.scope: Explicit non-null binary saturated context tree with exactly one infinite branch and no infinite shift-stable subtree. Its actual fixed alpha-LIS1 fair cascade series is summable, total<=2, but has no eventual C*r^n bound for any C>0 and 0<r<1 in the source Eq.(5) length grading. Bare universal convergence remains untouched.
entries.label: counterexample

entries.title: Two nested power-mean inequalities for the logarithm–arctangent mean
entries.scope: For all distinct positive real a,b, M(a,b)<Bp(M(a,Bq(a,b)),M(Bq(a,b),b)) for BOTH (p,q)=(sqrt17,(5-sqrt17)/2) and (-sqrt17,(5+sqrt17)/2), literal log-arctangent M and real power means.
entries.label: proof

entries.title: A negative H-eigenvalue of a reflected Steiner distance tensor
entries.scope: On the genuine star K1,29 at order4, M from minimum connected-subgraph edge count including repeated terminals and C1=M(.,.,.,(2J/30-I).) has a negative real first-free-index H-eigenpair. One counterexample refutes universal positivity.
entries.label: counterexample

entries.title: A 57-cell connected container for every fixed 11-omino
entries.scope: The connected integer-cell witness C={|x|+|y|<=5} minus {(2,2),(2,-2),(-2,2),(-2,-2)} has 57 cells and contains every fixed 11-omino by translation. Thus a(11)<=57<58, refuting the universal formula.
entries.label: counterexample

entries.title: Unbounded excess over the one-third edge-irregulator bound
entries.scope: For every integer t>=2, a connected simple graph with 6t+1 vertices and 8t edges has exact edge-irregulator minimum 3t. Hence no real absolute c>=1 satisfies I_e(G)<=|E(G)|/3+c for every connected finite simple graph.
entries.label: counterexample

entries.title: Failure of the exponential Rényi-increment threshold below one
entries.scope: For every real 0<p<1 there exists a finite normalized truncated exponential whose iid positive-sum Rényi entropy increment strictly exceeds the exponential increment. Consequently no threshold p0 in (0,1) has the proposed exponential-maximizer property above p0.
entries.label: counterexample

entries.title: There is no cubic 8-circulant nut graph: completing the existence classification of cubic polycirculant nut graphs
entries.scope: Bašić and Damnjanović, On cubic polycirculant nut graphs, arXiv:2411.16904v1 Conjecture 16 = Conjecture 1 of the published version (Comput. Appl. Math. 2025). Their Theorem 2 excludes l in {1,2,4,5} and constructs cubic l-circulant nut graphs for l in {3,6,7} and l >= 9; l = 8 was the only open case. Proof: a single kernel character on semiregular orbit coordinates gives a symmetric signed integral 8x8 quotient with nullity exactly one (injective lift) and nonzero diagonal cofactors; cubicity forces a local grammar; an inductive kernel-checked catalogue of 194 connected subcubic supports with 1,722 isomorphism certificates, 669 augmentations and tree switching reduce to 9,172 signed matrices, each excluded by an exact determinant (8,208) or zero principal cofactor (964) certificate. Valid for all orbit sizes m, without bounding graph order.
entries.label: proof

entries.title: A five-vertex counterexample to the nearest-colour contact-order conjecture for two-variable Cauchy transforms of coloured graphs
entries.scope: Tully-Doyle, Adlin, Thai and Tiscareno, Cauchy transforms of colored graphs in two variables, arXiv:2410.10695 (v1 2024, v2 2025), Conjecture 6.1: the contact order at the boundary point corresponding to (infinity, 0) equals twice the distance from the root to the nearest w-coloured vertex. False: the five-vertex graph with edges 01,02,03,13,24,34, root 0 and w-vertices 1,2 has nearest-w distance 1 but contact order 6 (analytic branches of exact orders 6 and 2; local maximum-branch convention of the source and of Bickel-Hong).
entries.label: counterexample

entries.title: Power-domination TAR uniqueness for complete bipartite graphs: PD^TAR(K_{s,t}) is unique if and only if s ≠ 2 and t ≠ 2
entries.scope: Bjorkman, Bozeman, Ferrero, Flagg, Grood, Hogben, Jacob and Reinhart, Power domination reconfiguration, arXiv:2201.01798, La Matematica 5 (2026): the uniqueness conjecture stated after Proposition p:K33 (still listed open in the Curtis-Flagg-Hogben survey arXiv:2406.05509v2, 2025). Proved: the new Core Theorem (for s,t >= 3, (s,t) != (3,3), K_{A,B} is the only graph on A ⊔ B with exactly its PD sets) via fort duality, pair forts, cross-degree rigidity isolating (3,3), two-sided completeness and independence; with the published TAR relabelling reduction (Bong-Carlson-Curtis-Haas-Hogben, Graphs Combin. 2023) formalized by a self-contained Hamming-isometry proof, and the source's small cases (K_2, K_{1,t}, K_{2,t} via K_{2,t}(e), K_{1,2} vs K_3, K_{3,3}) all formalized.
entries.label: proof

entries.title: A 15-vertex counterexample to the odd-kernel conjecture for io-decomposable Riordan graphs
entries.scope: Cheon, Jung, Kitaev and Mojallal, Riordan graphs II: Spectral properties, arXiv:1801.07021v1 (journal accepted manuscript in the Strathclyde repository retains it), Conjecture 7.7: for a singular io-decomposable Riordan graph G_n(g, zg), X_o = 0. False: g = 1+z+z^3+z^6+z^7+z^8+z^12+z^13 at n = 15 gives a connected io-decomposable Bell Riordan graph of nullity 1 whose kernel vector has odd part (-1,0,-1,0,1,0,1,1); the same graph arises from an infinite series satisfying the Lemma 2.11 identity at every index.
entries.label: counterexample

entries.title: Stable Kneser graphs violate the unit-gap diameter conjecture: D(SG(27,12)) ≥ 8 while D(SG(28,12)) ≤ 6
entries.scope: Ledezma, Pastine, Torres, Valencia-Pabon, arXiv:2112.01884v2 (DAM 350 (2024) 15-30), Conjecture 2. False at k = 12, r = 3: D(SG(27,12)) ≥ 8 by an explicit pair (masks 21669205, 39144021) with a distance-labelling certificate, and D(SG(28,12)) ≤ 6 by BFS-tree certificates over 116 rotation-orbit representatives; the drop is 2. Independent of the source's Theorem 6 (found false; the r = 2 route was a source-internal correction and is not credited).
entries.label: counterexample

entries.title: Gcd symmetry of recurrent-component sizes for the rotor network on the bidirected cycle (Chan-Levine Conjecture 8.3)
entries.scope: Chan and Levine, Abelian networks IV. Dynamics of nonhalting networks, arXiv:1804.03322 v1/v2; Mem. Amer. Math. Soc. 276 (2022), no. 1358, Conjecture 8.3: for the rotor network on the bidirected cycle C_n, n ≥ 3, m ≥ 1, the number of recurrent configurations in the unique recurrent component C_{n,m,i} of level m and weight i depends only on gcd(n, m, i). Proved for all n ≥ 3 and m ≥ 1, in the source's network language, with component existence and uniqueness proved.
entries.label: proof

entries.title: Valuation differences for coloured binary partitions: the full Ulas–Żmija Conjecture 6.1 picture (even formula, odd bounds, sharpness, and failure of per-colour sharpness for m ≡ 15 mod 16)
entries.scope: Ulas and Żmija, arXiv:1904.03398v1 (Ramanujan J. 55 (2021) 623–660), Conjecture 6.1 on ν2(c_m(4n) − c_m(n)) for m-coloured binary partitions. Proved in full: the even formula ν2 = ν2(n) + 2ν2(k) + 3 for m = 2k; the bounds +3 (m ≡ 1 mod 4) and +6 (m ≡ 3 mod 4) with nonzero differences; explicit infinite equality families for m ≡ 1 (mod 4) and m ≡ 3, 7, 11 (mod 16); and for m ≡ 15 (mod 16) the universal +7 bound, so equality never holds. Hence the conjecture is false under the per-k reading and true under the some-k reading.
entries.label: counterexample

entries.title: Equitable partitions of finite rectangular grids are symmetry orbits (Neuberger-Sieben-Swift Conjecture 5.6)
entries.scope: Neuberger, Sieben and Swift, arXiv:1908.05797 (SIAM J. Appl. Dyn. Syst. 19 (2020)), Conjecture 5.6, proved for all m, n >= 1: every equitable partition of P_m □ P_n is the orbit partition of a subgroup of the automorphism group; the equitable-partition lattice is isomorphic to the subgroup lattice exactly when a free vertex exists; and a free vertex exists unless 2 <= m = n <= 3.
entries.label: proof

entries.title: The stack-sorting degree grows faster than 1.80^n: a refutation of the Defant–Propp interval conjecture
entries.scope: Defant and Propp, arXiv:2002.07144 v3/v4 Conjecture 4.4 (Electron. J. Combin. 27(3) (2020) P3.51, Conjecture 23), restated as open by Defant (Adv. Math. 2022): the limit lies in (1.68, 1.73). False: every limit is at least 1.73 (Lean), and the exact values through n = 82 give at least 1.80468 (ordinary exact computation); the numerical value is about 1.95.
entries.label: counterexample

entries.title: A connected eight-vertex counterexample to strict increase of outer-connected domination under the middle-graph operation
entries.scope: Kazemnejad, Pahlavsay, Palezzato and Torielli, arXiv:2206.15439, Conjecture 7.1 (γ̃c(G) < γ̃c(M(G)) for every graph of order n >= 2). False already for connected graphs: G8 (8 vertices, 11 edges) has γ̃c(G8) = 4 = γ̃c(M(G8)) under both conventions. Credit only for the connected negation; the edgeless failure is a domain artefact.
entries.label: counterexample

entries.title: Five positive matchings for C_3 □ C_4: a finite counterexample to Conjecture 4.7 of arXiv:2502.02826
entries.scope: Farrokhi D. G. and Yazdan Pour, arXiv:2502.02826v1, Conjecture 4.7 (pmd(C_m □ C_n) = 6 for m + n even or (m, n) in {(3,4), (3,6), (5,6)}). False: C_3 □ C_4 has a five-part positive matching decomposition, and pmd(C_3 □ C_4) = 5 exactly; supporting certificates show pmd = 5 also at (3,5), (3,6) and (3,7).
entries.label: counterexample

entries.title: An eight-vertex counterexample to the Li–Weng rainbow vertex-disconnection Nordhaus–Gaddum conjecture (Conjecture 6.12 of arXiv:2004.06285v2)
entries.scope: Li and Weng, Further results on the rainbow vertex-disconnection of graphs, arXiv:2004.06285v2 Conjecture 6.12 (5.12 in v1; Bull. Malays. Math. Sci. Soc. 44 (2021)): rvd(G) + rvd(Ḡ) ≥ n for connected G, Ḡ of order n ≥ 8. False: an explicit connected 8-vertex graph G (masks 202,225,232,149,232,22,23,31) with connected complement has rvd(G) = 4 and rvd(Ḡ) = 3, sum 7. Supporting evidence: 74 of the 9,888 eligible order-8 isomorphism classes fail, and three connected one-vertex extensions fail at order 9 (sum 8 < 9), so the threshold is not merely off by one.

entries.title: One integral mapping-class orbit in every rank
entries.scope: For a closed oriented surface of genus g≥2 and r≥2, the deduction constructs an SL_r(O_L) representation whose character has Zariski-dense mapping-class orbit in the entire complex character variety. Mapping classes preserve O_L-valued representations; hence that orbit gives Zariski-dense integral points after a finite number-field extension. This treats closed curves and SL_r with no prescribed boundary monodromy. It does not settle the general Chevalley-group or arbitrary quasi-projective case. Rank two is credited to Coccia–Litt and antecedents.

entries.title: The sharp minimum multiplicity in a staircase tensor square
entries.scope: For the staircase ρ_m=(m,m−1,…,1), n=m(m+1)/2 and m≥2, the paper derives g(ρ_m,ρ_m,λ)≥m−1 for every λ other than (n) and (1^n), under its specified pinned cyclic-polytabloid source theorems. Equality occurs at λ=(n−1,1). The trivial and sign constituents have multiplicity one by self-duality and staircase self-conjugacy; m=1 is immediate. Thus the conditional estimate implies positivity for all constituents. The new deduction evaluates an inherited recursion; it is not an independent proof of the stipulated source theorems or an unconditional resolution of Saxl’s conjecture.
entries.label: partial_progress

entries.title: Removing the moment assumption from a stipulated planar no-bigeodesics theorem
entries.scope: Assuming the pinned planar no-bigeodesics theorem and its specified proof inputs, the paper removes the moment hypothesis for i.i.d. nearest-neighbor first-passage percolation on Z². It deduces absence of bigeodesics for every nonatomic distribution on finite nonnegative edge weights, with no direction restriction. The additional laws are precisely those for which the minimum of four independent weights has infinite second moment. The argument uses a dependent circuit cap, transfer of lifted limiting graphs and finite-energy replacements. It is a conditional extension, not an unconditional proof of the no-bigeodesics conjecture, and establishes nothing in higher dimensions.
entries.label: partial_progress

entries.title: Uniform interior gradient estimates for finite p through a constrained affine lift
entries.scope: Under the pinned infinity-harmonic regularity and fitted-class source inputs, the paper derives a dimension-dependent α_n∈(0,1/3] and C_n independent of finite p≥3, with ||Du||∞+[Du]_{C^{0,α_n}}≤C_n osc(u) on the interior half-ball for every bounded weak p-harmonic solution. For each fixed p>max{3,1+1/α_n}, α_n>1/(p−1), so the credited Lee–Lee transfer theorem gives C^{1,1/(p−1)} local regularity for bounded forcing. Constants in this corollary may depend on p. The manuscript states this consequence in its introduction. The threshold is nonexplicit and the intervening p range remains outside this result; the all-p conjecture is not settled.

entries.title: Disk rigidity for attained complete polynomial Crouzeix equality
entries.scope: For finite n,m≥1, A∈M_n(C), and a matrix polynomial F with coefficients in M_m(C), put M=max_{z∈W(A)}||F(z)|| and use F[A]=Σ A^k⊗C_k. Assuming the identified pinned source inputs, if M>0 and ||F[A]||=2M, then W(A) is a nondegenerate closed disk. The proof constructs a coefficient-space channel with polynomial boundary-unitary compression and rational exterior inverse, followed by a polynomial level-set rigidity argument. This concerns attained polynomial equality; it does not address nonattained suprema or arbitrary rational/holomorphic witnesses. The complete bound is a credited upstream premise. This is related equality-case progress, not an independent proof of the inequality asked here.
